title: A Simple General Approach to Inference About the Tail of a Distribution
question: How do you estimate how fat a tail is from the largest observations?
changed: The Hill estimator of the tail index, from the logs of the top order statistics.

title: Techniques for Verifying the Accuracy of Risk Measurement Models
question: How do you know whether a VaR model is right?
changed: Count the exceedances: a likelihood-ratio test that the breach rate matches the VaR level, with sobering power.

title: Evaluating Interval Forecasts
question: Is the right number of VaR breaches enough?
changed: Breaches must also be independent; a joint test of coverage and clustering catches models that react slowly.

title: Coherent Measures of Risk
question: What properties should any sensible risk measure have?
changed: Four axioms of coherence; VaR fails subadditivity, so merging two portfolios can raise it.

title: Optimization of conditional value-at-risk
question: Can portfolios be optimized for tail loss efficiently?
changed: Expected shortfall (CVaR) minimization becomes a linear program over scenarios, with VaR as a by-product.

title: Estimation of tail-related risk measures for heteroscedastic financial time series: an extreme value approach
question: How do you combine volatility clustering with fat tails in a risk forecast?
changed: Filter returns with GARCH, then fit extreme value theory to the standardized residuals' tail.

title: Extreme Correlation of International Equity Markets
question: Do correlations really rise in crashes?
changed: Using extreme value theory: correlation rises in large down markets but not in large up markets.

title: Correlation and Dependence in Risk Management: Properties and Pitfalls
venue: Risk Management: Value at Risk and Beyond (Cambridge University Press)
question: When does linear correlation mislead about joint risk?
changed: Outside elliptical distributions correlation can't describe dependence; copulas and tail dependence are needed.

title: CoVaR
question: How much does one institution's distress add to system-wide risk?
changed: ΔCoVaR: the system's VaR conditional on one institution being in distress, minus its median-state value.
